original_question: Is it consistent that the splitting number s is strictly larger than ℵ2 and that the strong polarized relation \( inom{s}{\omega} 	o  inom{s}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) still holds?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 2.3: the exact open problem asking whether it is consistent that the splitting number is above \aleph_2 while the positive strong polarized relation at \mathfrak{s} still holds.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact target almost verbatim: it uses the right invariant (the splitting number \mathfrak{s}), the right threshold (strictly above \aleph_2), and the right relation (the two-color strong polarized relation \binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2). This is precisely the question stated in Section 2 as Problem 2.3.
missing_details: State explicitly that \mathfrak{s} is the classical splitting number on \omega, not a generalized splitting number \mathfrak{s}_\kappa.

Unpack the partition relation so the question is stand-alone: for every coloring c:\mathfrak{s}\times\omega\to 2, there should exist A\subseteq\mathfrak{s} and B\subseteq\omega with |A|=\mathfrak{s} and |B|=\omega such that c restricted to A\times B is constant.
Make the ambient metamathematical quantifier explicit: 'Is it consistent with ZFC that ... ?'

If you want the paper-faithful scope made explicit, note that this asks about the boundary case \lambda=\mathfrak{s}; Theorem 1.6 already handles all \lambda<\mathfrak{s} with \operatorname{cf}(\lambda)\neq\omega, and the paper notes that the positive relation is already known when \mathfrak{s}=\aleph_2.
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that the classical splitting number \mathfrak{s} on \omega satisfies \mathfrak{s}>\aleph_2 and nevertheless every coloring c:\mathfrak{s}\times\omega\to 2 admits a monochromatic rectangle A\times B with A\subseteq\mathfrak{s}, B\subseteq\omega, |A|=\mathfrak{s}, and |B|=\omega; that is, \binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Section 2, Problem 2.3, not one of the background theorems from Section 1. Definition 0.1 provides the meaning of the strong polarized relation. The surrounding context in Section 2 says that the positive relation at \mathfrak{s} is known in the case \mathfrak{s}=\aleph_2, and Theorem 1.6 explains why this is a sharp boundary question: below the splitting number, the positive relation holds exactly when the upper cardinal has cofinality different from \omega. Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 are relevant background analogies for the continuum and for supercompact cardinals, but they are not the exact problem your draft is targeting.
